texts.facts: The Opposite Party No.1 / the Deputy Director of ESI Corporation before the Employees' Insurance Court is the appellant. The Application was filed by the 1 st respondent/applicant when the applicant received a notice demanding payment of a contribution of Rs.45,045/- for the period from 01.10.2012 to 30.04.2013 with respect to the establishment 'Hotel Nadan Ruchi'. His contention was that the establishment, 'Nadan Ruchi Restaurant', which was run by him, and the establishment 'Hotel Nadan Ruchi', run by the 2nd respondent/3rd opposite party, are two separate and distinct establishments. The application was allowed by the impugned Order holding that the establishment, 'Nadan Ruchi Restaurant' of the applicant and the establishment 'Hotel Nadan Ruchi' run by the 3rd opposite party are separate and distinct entities and directing the ESI corporation to refund the payment made by the applicant for the period from 01.10.2012 to 30.04.2013.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that even though the 3rd opposite party was there in the application, the 3rd opposite party is not shown in the impugned Order. There is no evidence before the EI Court to hold that the establishment of the applicant and the establishment of the 3rd opposite party are different. The EI Court entered certain findings even without any evidence. The learned counsel invited my attention to the findings of the EI court that the 3rd opposite party - employer employed a new set of employees after taking possession of the premises and that the applicant had no control or employment relation with the employees hired by the 3 rd opposite party. The EI court relied on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rashtriya Mill Mazdoor Sangh v. National Textile Corporation [(1996) 1 SCC 313], in which it is held that mere continuation of business in the same premises or similarity in the name does not make two establishments legally identical unless there is continuity in management, control, or employment.
